card.title: Resonance and transformers — AC at full power

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: AC voltage V₀sinωt meets three personalities: resistors obey instantly (in phase), inductors lag current by 90° (X_L = ωL), capacitors lead by 90° (X_C = 1/ωC). In series LCR they partially cancel — at resonance X_L = X_C, impedance bottoms at R, current peaks, and energy sloshes between L and C (LC oscillations at f₀ = 1/2π√LC). Transformers scale AC voltage by turns ratio (mutual induction); real ones leak flux, heat cores and windings.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: X_L = ωL · X_C = 1/ωC  ·  Z = √[R² + (X_L−X_C)²], I₀ = V₀/Z  ·  resonance: X_L = X_C → f₀ = 1/2π√(LC), Z = R, power max  ·  P_avg = V_rms·I_rms·cosφ, cosφ = R/Z  ·  transformer: V₂/V₁ = N₂/N₁ = I₁/I₂ (ideal)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Sinusoidal steady state assumed (phasor math); transients settled. Resonance needs series LCR driven at f₀ (parallel variants differ). Ideal-transformer ratios ignore losses, magnetising current and winding resistance — real efficiency η = output/input < 1.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Pure L or C draws ZERO average power (cosφ = 0 — wattless current). At resonance the circuit looks purely resistive. Step-up raises voltage for transmission (I²R losses fall as 1/V²); step-down delivers safe mains. LC tank without R would oscillate forever — radio tuning dials f₀.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Series LCR at resonance: net reactance X_L − X_C = 0 → Z = R (minimum) → I₀ = V₀/R (maximum), all source power dissipated in R (cosφ = 1). Off-resonance, current lags (inductive, X_L > X_C) or leads (capacitive) — the phasor triangle reads the phase at a glance.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Phasor analysis is steady-state sinusoidal only — square waves need Fourier. Real inductors carry resistance (Q-factor finite); real capacitors leak. Transformer ratios sag under load; DC cannot transform at all (no changing flux).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: LCR loop: V₀sinωt = IR + L(dI/dt) + Q/C — assume I = I₀sin(ωt−φ), substitute, match sine/cosine coefficients → Z and tanφ = (X_L−X_C)/R. Resonance dI₀/dω = 0 gives X_L = X_C. Transformer: same core flux links both coils → ε ∝ N per turn → V₂/V₁ = N₂/N₁; power conservation (ideal) gives the inverse current ratio.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Reactance ladder: DC → L short, C open; high f → L open, C short. Resonance checklist: X_L = X_C, Z = R, max current, cosφ = 1. Transformer: voltage follows turns, current opposes. Power questions: multiply by cosφ = R/Z.
